ch06.before: After more than three months of argument
ch06.alt: A group of villagers and cadres seated around a low table with teacups, talking, before a wall papered with newspapers.
ch06.caption: In the countryside during his work in Ningxia, winter 1969.

ch06.alt: Several men in winter coats and caps talking and smiling outdoors; the balding man at center is Chen Yangshan.
ch06.caption: Chen Yangshan (second from left) in Ningxia, 1972.

ch06.before: Chen Yangshan was accordingly restored to his former grade
ch06.alt: A formal group portrait of eleven older men in overcoats and Mao suits standing in two rows before a building.
ch06.caption: Chen Yangshan on his retirement in 1982, with leading members of the Supreme People's Procuratorate (front row, from left: Yu Ping, Huang Huoqing, Chen Yangshan, Zhang Su, Li Shiying). The names are the source's.

ch06.before: Referred to the Center, approval was given to quash
ch06.alt: Five older men in winter coats standing close together indoors, two of them shaking hands; one wears a beret.
ch06.caption: Chen Yun receiving Chen Yangshan and other Special Branch veterans, winter 1981 (first from left, Li Yimang; second from left, Chen Yangshan). The names are the source's.

ch06.before: Chen Yangshan was diligent in study
ch06.alt: An elderly couple seated outdoors before a wooden trellis; the woman in a white blouse, the balding man in a checked shirt.
ch06.caption: Chen Yangshan with his wife, Zhang Suzhen, convalescing at Qingdao, 1980.

ch06.alt: An elderly man in a dark jacket seated at a table behind two microphones, speaking.
ch06.caption: Chen Yangshan lecturing to cadres of the Zhejiang provincial state-security department at Hangzhou, 1987.

ch06.before: While he was lecturing, he heard that the daughter
ch06.alt: A seated portrait of an elderly balding man in a light jacket, smiling, in a garden.
ch06.caption: Chen Yangshan in his later years.

ch06.before: He charged the leaders of Ninghai County to see well
ch06.alt: A family group before a stone doorway; an elderly woman, an elderly man in dark clothes, and a younger man in a Mao suit stand in front.
ch06.caption: Visiting the family of the martyr Rou Shi during an inspection in Zhejiang, 1987 (front row: first from left, Rou Shi's daughter; second from left, Chen Yangshan). The labels are the source's.

ch06.before: From a shop clerk who believed in national salvation
ch06.alt: A large family group of some seventeen people of three generations posed indoors, with two small children holding flowers at the front.
ch06.caption: With his family on his eightieth birthday, 1986.

ch06.before: Chen Yangshan's life was indeed a hard one
ch06.alt: An elderly man seated in an armchair beside a side table bearing a bowl of fruit and a vase of flowers.
ch06.caption: Marking his eighty-fourth birthday in a ward at Beijing Hospital, October 7, 1989.

ch06.before: After Chen Yangshan died, the People's Daily published an article
ch06.alt: Four lines of handwritten Chinese calligraphy in ink, signed and dated.
ch06.caption: An inscription for Chen Yangshan by Li Qiang: 'A champion of the hidden front; a loyal and incorruptible public servant.' Dated November 24, 1992.

ch06.before: After Chen Yangshan died, the People's Daily published an article
ch06.alt: Two columns of cursive Chinese calligraphy in ink, signed and dated.
ch06.caption: An inscription for Chen Yangshan by Luo Qingchang, from Chen Yi's poem 'Green Pine': 'To know how nobly pure the pine, wait until the snows have melted.' Dated November 1992.

ch06.before: After Chen Yangshan died, the People's Daily published an article
ch06.alt: Several lines of handwritten Chinese calligraphy in ink with a red seal, signed and dated.
ch06.caption: An inscription in memory of Chen Yangshan by Liu Fuzhi: 'A lifetime of revolution; his light shines on those who follow.' Dated August 2006.

ch06.before: After Chen Yangshan died, the People's Daily published an article
ch06.alt: Two large columns of Chinese calligraphy in ink with a smaller inscription and a red seal.
ch06.caption: An inscription for Chen Yangshan by Ling Yun: 'Green pine and emerald cypress; bones of iron, a heart of cinnabar.' Dated summer 2003.
